what: Prudential Financial sells life insurance, annuities and retirement products in the United States, Japan and emerging markets, and runs PGIM, an asset manager with over $1.6 trillion under management.
customers: Individuals buying life insurance and annuities, employers arranging group benefits and pension transfers, and institutions investing through PGIM.
money: insurance in Japan and emerging markets
moat: A balance sheet large enough to take on corporate pension obligations, a business where very few competitors can participate.
risks: Falling interest rates reduce the income earned on invested premiums
Japanese operations expose it to yen movements
Revenue fell about 14% last year on insurance accounting effects
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
opportunities: A dividend yield above 4.5% with a long increase record
Pension risk transfer demand continues as companies offload obligations
PGIM earns fees without consuming insurance capital
watch: PGIM net flows and the sales of annuities and pension transfers.
